A few months ago, I was visiting a city I didn't know very well, and I decided to take the bus instead of a taxi, just to save some money on a trip that was already getting expensive.
I looked up the number online, walked to the stop, and waited, feeling pretty proud of myself for figuring out the local transit.
A bus came, and the number looked right, so I got on without really checking the destination sign above the windshield.
I mean, it was close enough, and I figured buses in the same area probably went to similar places anyway.
That was my first mistake, and honestly, it wouldn't be my last one of the day.
I sat down, looked out the window, and just relaxed for a while, watching the streets go by.
The city started to look a little different, quieter, less crowded, but I told myself it was just a part of town I hadn't seen yet.
Twenty minutes passed.
Then thirty.
And the buildings kept getting fewer and fewer until there was almost nothing left.
Eventually, the bus pulled into a small station, and the driver announced the last stop.
I looked around, and there was nothing familiar at all.
No hotel, no landmarks, nothing I recognized from my map.
I was, as far as I could tell, in the middle of nowhere, with a phone that barely had any signal.
I got off the bus and just stood there for a second, trying to figure out what to do next.
So I walked into a small shop nearby and asked the guy behind the counter if he spoke English, hoping for the best.
He didn't, not really, but he pulled out his own phone and used a translation app to help me figure out where I was.
Turns out, I'd gotten on a bus with almost the same number, but it went in a totally different direction.
Classic mistake, apparently a common one for tourists in that part of the city.
He was kind enough to walk me to the right stop and even waited with me until the correct bus showed up.
I offered to pay him for his time, but he just waved his hand and said something that I'm pretty sure meant, "Don't worry about it."
Two hours later than planned, I finally made it back to my hotel.
My feet hurt, I was starving, and I'd seen a part of the city I never would have found on purpose.
Honestly, it turned out to be one of the more memorable afternoons of the whole trip, even if it wasn't exactly the plan.
